faqs.question: I am unable to connect my product to a wireless network. What should I do?
faqs.answer: The printer does not come with built-in wireless features and does not support a wireless (or Ethernet) connection to a network router. Only a direct wired connection to the computer is supported.

faqs.question: How do I obtain the latest product software for Windows or my Mac?
faqs.answer: You can download the latest product driver from the Downloads section of this website.

faqs.question: Does Epson have a program where I can donate my working electronic equipment?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Epson America, Inc. and
Digitunity
have joined together with the goal of helping those who are facing economic challenges or have a disability to gain access to today's technology. With your donation, you not only help the environment, but you also help change the lives of those who need these products the most.

faqs.question: How do I change the font size of text when I print from software in Windows?
faqs.answer: You need to select the text or font size in the software you are printing from, not the printer driver. For detailed instructions, contact the company for the application you are printing from.

faqs.question: I brought my product with me to a different country and can't find ink for it. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Some Epson printers and ink cartridges are specific to a regional market and not sold worldwide, although the same printers are sold in the U.S. and Canada. If you have a printer sold in the U.S. or Canada, you may not be able to easily get ink cartridges for it in foreign markets.
Unfortunately, because of customs and tax regulations, the Epson E-Stores in the U.S. and Canada are unable to ship to addresses outside the U.S. and Canada.

faqs.question: When I try to print to my product in Windows 7, printing is slow or my product stops printing. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Try the following:
Select a lower quality setting in the printer software.
Make sure your system meets the minimum system requirements for your printer.
Close the
Devices and Printers
window before you print.
Clear space on your hard drive or run a defragmentation utility.
Close programs that you're not using.
Increase your system's memory.

faqs.question: Does OS X support manual duplex printing with my product?
faqs.answer: This feature is not supported in Mac OS X. However, if your printer has a built-in automatic duplexer, auto-duplexing is supported in Mac OS X 10.6 (Snow Leopard).

faqs.question: Can the Epson ink cartridges be refilled or can I use third-party ink cartridges without voiding the warranty?
faqs.answer:
Epson does not recommend refilling or using other brands of ink cartridges.  Epson uses a permanent Micro Piezo print head that has allowed Epson to lead the industry in delivering consistent photo image quality by using variable-sized droplets.  Micro Piezo print head can also use a wider variety of inks, which has allowed Epson to introduce such ink breakthroughs as DURABrite® and Epson UltraChrome® inks that offer greatly improved humidity resistance, smudge resistance, and fade resistance.
Using refilled ink cartridges will not void the product's original warranty; however, if these products cause a failure, the repair of that failure will not be covered under warranty.

faqs.question: Web pages don't print the way they appear on my monitor. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
The pages may not print correctly due to the web page design. Try the following:
Check for a
Printer-friendly Version
(or similarly named) option on the web page.
Change the page setup and paper size settings, and select the preview option in your browser to check the changes before you print.

faqs.question: I installed new ink cartridges and my product seems to be doing a long cleaning cycle. Is this normal?
faqs.answer:
When an ink cartridge is installed in the printer, it will take about a half a minute to charge the ink system and initialize the printer. While the ink is charging the
power light flashes. Never turn off the printer while the
power light is flashing (unless the printer hasn't moved or made noise for more than 5 minutes). This initialization is a normal and necessary process. If the printer initialization does not stop after 5 minutes turn the printer off and contact Epson technical support for assistance.

faqs.question: How long should an ink cartridge remain in my product if it's not used often?
faqs.answer: When an installed ink cartridge is more than six (6) months old, you may need to replace it if you notice that your printouts don't look as good as they used to. If print quality doesn't improve after cleaning and aligning the print head, you should replace the ink cartridges.

faqs.question: How do I know when an ink cartridge needs to be replaced?
faqs.answer:
When the ink replace light is on, the printer will require you to change the cartridge. You need to replace a cartridge when it's expended or it gets too old.  See
Replacing an Ink Cartridge
.

faqs.question: How do I replace an ink cartridge?
faqs.answer:
See
Replacing an ink cartridge
.

To ensure good results, use genuine Epson ink cartridges and do not refill them. Other products may cause damage to your printer not covered by Epson's warranty.

The high capacity cartridges are recommended as the usual replacement cartridges for this printer based on the anticipated printing frequency of typical purchasers. Users that print infrequently may want to choose the standard capacity cartridges that are also compatible with this printer.

faqs.question: A color ink cartridge is expended even though I print in black only. Why does this happen?
faqs.answer:
To keep the print head clear and ready to print, the printer uses a small amount of ink from all the cartridges whenever it prints.   Even if you select
Black ink Only
, some color ink is still being used.

faqs.question: Can the printer still print if an ink cartridge is expended or not installed?
faqs.answer: No. The printer will not operate if any cartridge is expended or removed. It's best to always have extra cartridges on hand.

faqs.question: How can I stop my product from feeding multiple pages at the same time?
faqs.answer:
If multiple pages feed, follow these steps:
Remove the paper from the sheet feeder.
Fan the edges of the sheets.
Reload them against the right side of the feeder.
Slide the left edge guide snugly, but not too tightly, against the paper. Don't load paper above the arrow mark on the left edge guide and make sure it is under the tabs on the left and right edge guides.
If that doesn't help, make sure the paper you're using is not too thin or too thick. If it is very humid, the paper may have absorbed moisture and should be replaced with dry paper. If necessary, try different paper from a new package. Check the
Paper specifications
in the User's Guide for ranges of paper size and thickness you can print with, as well as environmental requirements.

faqs.question: Sometimes the paper doesn't eject all the way or is wrinkled. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Make sure the correct paper size is selected in your application and/or printer software. If the paper doesn't eject fully, it may be too long for the printer. If the paper is wrinkled, the paper may be damp or too thin. Check the
Paper specifications
in the User's Guide for ranges of paper size and thickness you can print with, as well as environmental requirements.

faqs.question: My product won't feed paper. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
If paper won't feed, follow these steps:
Remove the paper from the sheet feeder.
Fan the edges of the sheets.
Reload the sheets against the right side of the feeder. Make sure the paper stack is leaning against the sheet feeder and not standing straight up.
Slide the left edge guide snugly, but not too tightly, against the paper. Don't load paper above the arrow mark on the left edge guide and make sure it is under the tabs on the left and right edge guides.

faqs.question: What is the correct way to load transparency paper?
faqs.answer:
For best results, use
Epson Ink Jet Transparencies
. Before loading the transparency, place the included support sheet or a sheet of plain paper beneath the transparency (or beneath the stack of transparencies if you are loading more than one). You can load up to 20 transparencies at a time, but if you have more than one transparency loaded, the minimum top margin you can use is 1.2 inches. Also, you may get better results by loading one sheet at a time. Insert the transparency sheet making sure that the notch is at the top right side of the sheet. Remember to
select the correct paper type
in the printer software.

faqs.question: What kind of paper gives the best results for high quality printing?
faqs.answer:
For best results, Epson recommends using
Epson Premium Bright White Paper
,
Epson Matte Paper Heavyweight
,
Epson Premium Semigloss Photo Paper
and
Epson DuraBrite Ink Glossy Photo Paper
.

faqs.question: Does the type of paper I use really make a difference?
faqs.answer:
This printer will work with a variety of papers and media, but for best results it is important to use paper that works best with Epson's long-lasting and water-resistant DuraBrite pigmented inks.
Epson matte paper,
Epson Premium Semigloss Photo Paper
and
Epson DuraBrite Ink Glossy Photo Paper
have been developed to produce the highest-quality output with DuraBrite inks. For optimum image quality and longest print life (up to 70 years), print your photos with Epson's
Matte Paper Heavyweight
.
Other brands of paper may not work best with DuraBrite inks. These papers may give you lower-quality color images and they will not have the longevity of Epson's long-lasting media. The ink may also not dry properly.

faqs.question: Can I use sheet labels with my product?
faqs.answer: No.

faqs.question: Heavy coated or thick paper does not load correctly or loads skewed. What should I do?
faqs.answer: The paper you are using may be too heavy or glossy for the paper roller to pick up. Be sure the paper is within printer specifications.

faqs.question: My printout has incorrect margins. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
If margins are incorrect, the problem could be due to a software setting or the paper may be loaded incorrectly. See
The margins are incorrect
.
If you're printing from a web browser, especially when viewing web pages using frames, the pages may not print correctly due to the web page design. This is not the fault of the printer or printer setup. Often there is nothing that you can do to print the complete page as displayed. Check to see if there is a
Printer Friendly Version
(or similarly-named) icon or link on the web page that you can click on. Also, try a different web browser or a newer version (if available) to see if that helps.

faqs.question: My printouts are missing color and/or black print. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
If color or black is missing, the problem could be due to a software setting (the printer software or your application may have been set to print black only) or the printer's condition. See
You see wrong or missing colors
.

faqs.question: The image look inverted, as if viewed in a mirror. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
You may have accidentally used the
Mirror Image
or
Flip Horizontal
option in the printer driver or a similar feature in your software application. Turn off the setting in the printer driver and/or application and try printing again.

faqs.question: The quality of my printed output is unacceptable. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Make sure you're using the correct driver for your printer.  If that doesn't help, the problem could be due to a software setting or printer's condition. See
Print Quality Problems
.

faqs.question: My product is printing blank pages from Windows or my Mac. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Make sure your printer is selected in the
Print
window (Windows) or in the
Page Setup
and
Print
windows (Mac OS X), or is the active printer in the Chooser (Mac OS 8.6 to 9.x).
Your document may have more pages than you think. Select
Print Preview
from your application's
File
menu before printing. Then either select to print only the current page, or only those pages with text, or delete the extra pages in your document before printing.
Paper settings in the printer software may be incorrect for your paper size. Check the paper size, orientation, printable area, and layout settings to make sure they're correct for your paper size.
If these suggestions don't help, the print head nozzles may be clogged. See
Cleaning the Print Head
.

faqs.question: My printout has lines running through it. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
The problem could be due to a software setting or printer's condition. See
You see banding
.

faqs.question: My product sounds as though it is printing, but nothing prints. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
The problem could be due to your printer's position or condition. See
more information
.

Check for a

faqs.question: Can my product be set up to print in black by default instead of color?
faqs.answer:
If you're using Windows, you can set up the printer to print in black by default.  Follow the steps below:
Right-click the
printer icon in the lower right corner of your screen (taskbar).
Select
Printer Settings
. A preferences window will appear.
Click the
Advanced
button in the lower right corner of the preferences window (if you see a
Basic
button in the lower right corner of the window, skip this step).
Click the
Black Ink Only
check box.
Click
OK
in the preferences window.
If you're using a Macintosh, you can't set up the printer to print in black by default.

faqs.question: How do I select the print resolution in the Windows software?
faqs.answer:
Rather than selecting the print resolution in the driver, you select the following types of documents and the resolution will be automatically selected depending on the paper type you choose to print on:
Draft
: For rough drafts with reduced print quality
Text
: For text-only documents with higher text quality
Text & Image
: For documents with text and images with higher quality
Photo
: For photos and graphics with good quality and speed
Best Photo
: For photos or graphics with high print quality

faqs.question: When printing in Windows, how can I prevent an extra page from being ejected after every print job?
faqs.answer:
The Separator Page function may be enabled. Follow these steps to disable it:
Click
Start
or
.
Do one of the following:
Windows XP
:
Select
Printers and Faxes
(or select
Settings
, then select
Printers and Faxes
).
Windows Vista
:
Select
Control Panel
, then
Printer
or
Printers
under Hardware and Sound
.
Windows 7
:
Select
Control Panel
, then
View Devices and Printers
under Hardware and Sound.
In the
Printers
or
Printers and Faxes
window, right-click on your printer's name.
Select
Properties
, click the Advanced tab, then press the
Separator Page
button.
In the Separator Page window, delete the information in the text box and then click
OK
.
Click
OK
again.

faqs.question: My product is suddenly printing slowly after heavy use. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
If the printer becomes overheated after excessive use, it will slow down to prevent damage. If you notice this, please wait until the green
power light is on solid and not flashing. Then, turn off the printer and allow it to cool. Normal speed should resume after cooling.
